title: slo-stress-harness-telemetry-replay-and-synthetic-load-2027
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview:
This document describes the SLO Stress Harness: a repeatable, auditable system for validating SLO detection, exercising error-budget workflows, and verifying capacity/fallback behavior for multi-tenant model inference. The harness combines two capabilities: (1) telemetry replay (replaying historical traces/metrics/logs into our observability pipeline) and (2) synthetic load generation (tenant-shaped request generators with configurable fidelity).

Goals:
- Verify SLO alert correctness (thresholds, silence windows, deduplication).
- Exercise automated error-budget escalation and throttling paths.
- Validate capacity autoscaling and graceful degradation under realistic tenant mixes.
- Produce evidence artifacts that satisfy post-incident review standards.

Scope and non-goals:
- Included: model-serving latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), availability SLOs, embedding throughput SLOs, tenant-priority throttles, scoreboard evidence generation.
- Excluded: application-layer feature correctness (business logic), security penetration tests, and production customer data mutation.

Terminology:
- Replay run: executing historical telemetry through the observability pipeline while keeping production services isolated from test actions.
- Synthetic cohort: a set of virtual tenants with traffic profiles and token distributions.
- Evidence bundle: time-series, raw replay events, alert screenshots, and run metadata attached to the post-run artifact.

System components:
- replay-agent (service): consumes archived traces (traceproto, JSON events) and publishes them into the telemetry bus with original timestamps or time-shifted windows.
- synthetic-driver (CLI/service): generates HTTP/gRPC inference requests following tenant profiles and can target canary or dedicated pools.
- orchestrator (k8s CronJob + Step Function): coordinates run lifecycle, snapshot creation, and artifact collection.
- artifact-collector: archives evidence bundles to S3 (rdw-run-evidence/<run-id>) and marks retention metadata.

SLOs and error budgets used in tests (examples):
- API Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly (error budget: 21.6 minutes/month).
- Latency SLOs (text generation, 16k context): p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms.
- Embedding throughput SLO (batching workloads): 90% of batches complete < 120ms.

Escalation thresholds for drills and automation (mirror production policy):
- Green: burn < 20% — no human intervention.
- Yellow: burn >= 20% and < 50% — paging to oncall, begin capacity hedging.
- Red: burn >= 50% — immediate throttle controls and canary rollback if applicable.

Test matrix (summary table):
| Scenario | Primary objective | Input artifact | Expected outcome |
|---------|------------------|----------------|------------------|
| Telemetry replay: high-burst holidays | Verify detection and alerting for real-world burst shapes | 2026-12-24-traces.json.gz | Alerts trigger, evidence bundle contains replayed traces, no production traffic impact |
| Synthetic tenant-mix (10% heavy, 90% light) | Validate autoscaler shape & fair-share | tenant-mix-v2.yaml | Autoscaler scales to headroom threshold; lower-priority tenants throttle gracefully |
| Steady p99 drift | Validate regression detection | latency-drift-2026.json | SLO regression alerting (ticket created + evaluation run) |
| Combined replay + synthetic | End-to-end SLO guardrails | combined-run-manifest.json | Orchestrator triggers throttles and archives evidence; simulated customer impact documented |

Test data and replay manifest examples:
- Replay manifest (JSON):
{
  "run_id": "replay-2027-02-03-01",
  "source_bucket": "rdw-telemetry-archive",
  "objects": [
    "2026/12/24/trace-session-abc123.json.gz",
    "2026/12/24/metrics-run-abc123.prom.json"
  ],
  "time_shift_minutes": 0,
  "inject_alert_markers": true
}

- Tenant profile YAML (excerpt):
cohorts:
  - name: heavy-realtime
    rps: 12
    avg_tokens: 2000
    burst_pattern: [30s, 5m]
    priority: high
  - name: light-background
    rps: 40
    avg_tokens: 64
    priority: best-effort

Runbook: SLO drill execution steps (playbook)
1. Prepare run context
   - Owner: eng-sre oncall and product infra steward.
   - Create a new run in the orchestrator UI, set run_id and description.
   - Verify isolation: target a test namespace or canary pool. Do not run against shared production pools unless run is explicitly authorized in the change calendar.
2. Stage artifacts
   - Place replay artifacts in rdw-telemetry-archive/<run-id>/ and register in replay manifest.
   - Upload tenant profile to rdw-test-configs/<run-id>/cohort.yaml.
3. Dry-run validation (10–15 minutes)
   - Execute replay-agent in dry-run mode (no outward publish) to assert payload compatibility. Fix schema mismatches.
   - Run synthetic-driver with a single low-priority cohort for 5 minutes to validate client credentials and endpoints.
4. Execute run
   - Start orchestrator: record start timestamp.
   - Monitor key dashboards: SLO-dashboard (p95/p99), error-rate, resource utilization (GPU/host CPU/memory), autoscaler events.
   - Ensure artifact-collector is streaming logs to evidence bucket.
5. Mid-run checks (first 15 minutes)
   - Confirm that alerting rules fired as expected: check alert history and deduplication.
   - Check automated throttles: if throttle triggers, confirm lower-priority cohorts are impacted first.
6. Wind-down and evidence collection
   - Stop synthetic-driver and replay-agent in orchestrator.
   - Collect evidence bundle: dashboards screenshots, alerts exported to JSON, raw replay events, driver logs, and autoscaler decision logs.
   - Tag the run with findings: pass/fail and any anomalies.
7. Post-run review
   - Owner opens a post-run review document within 48 hours containing the evidence bundle link, summary, and remediation plan.
   - If error-budget burn crossed Yellow/Red thresholds, follow incident-review standards (attach run evidence to incident).

Automations and CI integration:
- Example GitHub Actions job that schedules a monthly SLO smoke-run (YAML snippet):
name: slo-smoke
on: schedule
  cron: '0 6 1 * *' # first day of month at 06:00 UTC
jobs:
  schedule-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Trigger orchestrator run
        run: |
          curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.SLO_RUNNER_TOKEN }}" \n            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n            -d '{"manifest": "s3://rdw-test-configs/monthly-smoke.json", "tag": "monthly-smoke"}' \n            https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/runs

- Evidence retention policy:
  - Keep run evidence for 180 days by default.
  - If run escalated to incident, keep for 3 years. Artifact-collector enforces S3 lifecycle rules.

Failure modes and mitigation guidance:
- Missing telemetry fields during replay:
  - Symptom: replay-agent logs schema errors and metrics drop.
  - Mitigation: run schema-converter (tools/replay/schema-normalizer) and rerun dry-run.
- False positives from replayed alerts (alert flapping):
  - Symptom: alert flood during replay vs. production baseline.
  - Mitigation: enable replay-annotation to tag alerts as "test-run"; use deduplication window and adjust team notification routing to suppress noise.
- Autoscaler oscillation during synthetic bursts:
  - Symptom: scale-up/scale-down thrash causing latency spikes.
  - Mitigation: increase stabilization window and tune CPU/GPU headroom settings in autoscaler policy. Documented tuning parameters below.

Key configuration table (autoscaler tuning defaults for tests):
| setting | default (test harness) | production recommendation |
|---------|-----------------------:|-------------------------:|
| min_replicas | 2 | align to service-criticality |
| max_replicas | 20 | based on committed capacity |
| scale_up_threshold | 0.75 (utilization) | 0.85 |
| scale_down_threshold | 0.45 | 0.5 |
| stabilization_window_sec | 120 | 300 |

Evidence and post-run artifact checklist:
- run-id and manifest (JSON)
- raw replay events (gzipped)
- synthetic-driver logs and payload samples
- alert export (JSON) and timeline screenshot
- autoscaler event log and vertical-scaling decisions
- run summary (pass/fail + short description)
- remediation actions (if any)

Ownership, cadence, and scheduling:
- Routine: monthly smoke runs automated by CI.
- Advisory: quarterly full-fidelity replay runs with cross-team participation (SRE, product infra, and model owning team).
- Owners:
  - Run steward: eng-sre (primary oncall)
  - Evidence curator: reliability-ops rotation
  - Tooling ownership: infra-tooling team

Compliance and safety notes:
- Do not include PII or raw customer prompts in replay artifacts unless redacted. Use replay-anonymizer before staging artifacts.
- For runs that interact with dedicated customer pools, obtain written approval and schedule a maintenance window.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands
- Validate manifest syntax:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @manifest.json https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/manifest/validate
- Start a local dry-run of replay-agent:
  replay-agent --manifest manifest.json --dry-run --out debug.log
- Collect evidence into artifacts directory:
  orchestrator-cli collect-evidence --run-id replay-2027-02-03-01 --out ./evidence/replay-2027-02-03-01.tgz
